root hairs and primary xylem
Casparian strips and conjunctive tissue
lateral branches of stem and cork cambium
questions.solution:
In a dicotyledonous root, the pericycle is the layer of cells located just inside the endodermis. According to NCERT, the initiation of lateral roots and the vascular cambium during secondary growth takes place in these pericycle cells.

Root hairs arise exogenously from the outermost layer (epiblema). Casparian strips are a characteristic feature of the endodermis, not the pericycle. Lateral branches of stems have an exogenous origin, unlike the endogenous origin of lateral roots from the pericycle.

questions.question: In a young dicot stem, the intrafascicular cambium is located :
options: Between two adjacent vascular bundles
Between primary xylem and primary phloem
Between pericycle and endodermis
Between secondary xylem and secondary phloem
questions.solution:
In a young dicot stem, the vascular bundles are open, meaning they contain a strip of cambium within them. This cambium, present inherently inside the vascular bundle between the primary xylem and primary phloem, is called the intrafascicular (or fascicular) cambium.

The cambium that forms between two adjacent vascular bundles is the interfascicular cambium. Secondary xylem and secondary phloem are tissues produced later by the activity of the continuous cambial ring.

Answer: Between primary xylem and primary phloem
